sources.entry: RISC-V Vector Extension, Version 1.0 - The ratified vector ISA, shipped only as IP and chiplets, pending a socketed server part and a run against Arm or x86.

summary.title: 30.1. "V" Standard Extension for Vector Operations, Version 1.0
summary.one_liner: The RISC-V "V" vector extension spec defines ELEN/VLEN parameters, vector registers, vtype/vl/vstart CSRs, LMUL grouping, and tail/mask agnostic policies.
takeaways: VLEN and ELEN are per-hart parameters; VLEN must be a power of 2 and at most 2^16.
vtype encodes SEW (vsew) and LMUL (vlmul), and only vset*vl* instructions can change it.
LMUL can be fractional (1/8 to 1/2), letting mixed-width data use all 32 vector registers.
Tail and inactive elements can be undisturbed or agnostic; vsetvli requires ta/tu and ma/mu flags.
Mismatched VLEN or ELEN between harts complicates migrating threads with active vector state.
summary.summary: This is the normative RISC-V "V" vector extension specification, version 1.0, from the RISC-V documentation site. The excerpt covers implementation-defined parameters (ELEN, VLEN), the programmer's model (32 vector registers and the vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, vtype, vl, and vlenb CSRs), and how mstatus/vsstatus VS fields track vector state. It then goes into vtype fields, SEW and LMUL encodings with VLMAX tables, and the tail-agnostic and mask-agnostic policies. The text is reference-style, with rationale notes explaining design choices. The page is a partial view and ends in the middle of the vxrm section.
